title: A PLIED TWISTED CAP PLY REINFORCEMENT HYBRID YARN
abstract: The present invention relates to a cap ply reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) which is located between the tread and the belt package especially in radial passenger vehicle tires, which improves the high speed durability of the tire by using polyamide (N)/polyester (P) yarns, and which provides fuel saving by decreasing the rolling resistance.
claims:
CLAIMS1.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) forming the layer located between the tread and the belt package in the pneumatic radial tire comprising the said tread and belt package, comprised of at least two yarns, obtained by plied twisting of the said yarns together, and characterized in that one of the said yarns is aliphatic polyamide (N), and the other one is polyester, and the ratio of the polyester (P) in the said polyester (P) yarn is minimum 90% by weight, and the ratio of the aliphatic polyamide (N) in the said aliphatic polyamide (N) yarn is minimum 90% by weight.

 2.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim    1, characterized in that the said aliphatic polyamide (N) yarn is nylon, and the said polyester (P) yarn in polyethylene terephthalate (PET).

 3.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim    2, characterized in that nylon 6.6 is used as the said aliphatic polyamide (N) yarn.

 4.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim 2, characterized in that nylon 6 is used as the said aliphatic polyamide (N) yarn.

 5.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim 2, characterized in that the content of the said aliphatic polyamide (N) yarn is comprised of a blend of nylon 6.6 and nylon 6.

 6.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim 1, characterized in that the linear densities of each one of the saidaliphatic polyamide (N) and the said polyester (P) yarns are in a range of 200-3000 dtex.

 7.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim 1, characterized in that the difference between linear densities of each one of the said aliphatic polyamide (N) and the said polyester (P) yarns is maximum 20%.

 8.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim 1, characterized in that the pre-twisting levels of the said aliphatic polyamide (N) and the said polyester (P) yarns are zero.

 9.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim 1, characterized in that the pre-twisting levels of each one of the said aliphatic polyamide (N) and the said polyester (P) yarns are maximum 100 tpm.

 10.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (9) according to claim 9, characterized in that the pre-twisting directions of the said aliphatic polyamide (N) and the said polyester (P) yarns are same, in any one of Z or S twisting directions.

 11.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (1) according to claim 1, characterized in that the combined pre-twisting level of the said aliphatic polyamide (N) and the said polyester (P) yarns is in range of 100-    500 tpm.

 12.   A cap ply plied twisted reinforcement hybrid yarn (11) according to claim 1, characterized in that the combined pre-twisting level of the said aliphatic polyamide (N) and the said polyester (P) yarns is in range of 150-    250 tpm.

title: HYBRIDCORD AND TIRE COMPRISING THE SAME
abstract: The present invention relates to a hybrid cord and a tire comprising the same. The hybrid cord comprises: a core comprising a polyamide 66 cord of 600 to 900 denier; and a covering twisted helically about the core and comprising an aramid cord of 600 to 900 denier. The hybrid cord can reduce tire noise, enhance ride comfort, durability, and steering stability, and reduce rolling resistance by lightening a cap ply.

ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the challenge of achieving optimal performance in hybrid cords and tires while minimizing noise, improving ride comfort, durability, and steering stability. Traditional hybrid cords, which combine aramid and polyamide 66 cords, are often used in high-performance tires but result in increased tire weight, which negatively impacts fuel efficiency and environmental sustainability. Additionally, these cords exhibit poor processability and high initial modulus, leading to reduced noise and ride comfort at high speeds. The invention aims to solve these issues by creating a hybrid cord that reduces weight, enhances performance, and maintains the desired properties without compromising the tire's structural integrity.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The hybrid cord is produced by combining a polyamide 66 cord of greater than 600 denier to 900 denier with an aramid cord of greater than 600 denier to 900 denier. The aramid cord is spirally twisted about the core, while the polyamide 66 cord is positioned closer to the core. The twisting process involves a lower lead with a twist number of 200 TPM to 500 TPM, with the polyamide 66 cord having a lower twist number. The hybrid cord is then heat-treated with a controlled unwinding speed, where the polyamide 66 cord is thermally contracted by increasing the unwinding speed compared to the winding speed. This ensures the polyamide 66 cord is closer to the central axis, while the aramid cord is wound around the outside. The hybrid cord is applied to the tire's reinforcement layers, particularly the cap ply, to reduce rolling resistance and improve noise reduction. The hybrid cord is designed to have an initial modulus of 5 g/D to 20 g/D and a high load modulus of 50 g/D to 300 g/D, with a gradient density (EPI) of 30 EPI to 37 EPI. The hybrid cord is composed of 15 wt% to 85 wt% aramid and 85 wt% to 15 wt% polyamide 66, with the aramid cord having a tensile strength of 18 g/D to 35 g/D and a Young's modulus of 200 g/D to 500 g/D. The hybrid cord is applied to the tire's cap ply, where it reduces the weight of the tire by several hundred grams, thereby improving fuel efficiency and reducing environmental impact.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention provides a hybrid cord and tire that significantly reduces tire weight while maintaining high performance, noise reduction, and improved ride comfort. The hybrid cord, composed of lower fineness aramid and polyamide 66 cords, enhances high-speed durability and steering stability without compromising the tire's structural integrity. The specific twisting configuration ensures better processability and reduces the thickness of the rolled material, leading to a more efficient manufacturing process. The hybrid cord exhibits excellent adhesion and maintains high load modulus, making it suitable for high-performance radial tires. Additionally, the hybrid cord allows for a more environmentally friendly approach by reducing material usage and weight, meeting societal and consumer demands for eco-friendly vehicles. The invention also improves the tire's ability to handle high-speed conditions while maintaining low rolling resistance, making it a superior alternative to traditional hybrid cords.

title: A CAP PLY REINFORCEMENT STRIP FOR PNEUMATIC TIRES
abstract: The present invention relates to a cap ply reinforcement strip in pneumatic tire (1) which is ready-to-use plain woven and comprised of warps (3) and cotton wefts (2). The inventive cap ply reinforcement strip in pneumatic tires (1) eliminates calendering and strip preparation steps, and enables to decrease the rolling resistance of the tire.
claims:
CLAIMS1.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1), which is wound spirally on the belt package of a radial tire such that it will have 0° to 5° with the equatorial plane and it is in direct contact with the tread rubber, comprising warp yarns (3) and cotton weft yarns (2) wherein surface of the said strip is dipped with an adhesive material characterized in that    - the plurality of the said cotton weft yarns (2) parallel to each other wherein the linear density of which changes between 400 and 2000 dtex, and    the said adhesive material content on the said strip surface is at least    10% and maximum 60% by weight.

 2.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to claim 1 characterized by the linear density values of the said cotton weft yarns (2) are between 600 to 1500 dtex.

 3.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims characterized by the said cotton yarns (2) used as weft are twisted or non-twisted.

 4.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims characterized by the number of the said cotton weft yarns (2) in a 10 cm long strip (1) is between 5 to 50, preferably 10 to 20.

 5.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to claim 1-2, characterized in by the said adhesive material is RFL (Resorcinol Formaldehyde Latex).

 6.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to claim 1-2, characterized by the said adhesive material does not contain any resorcinol formaldehyde (Resorcinol Formaldehyde Free).

 7.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims, characterized by said adhesive material content is between preferably 10% to 40 or more preferably 10% to 25% by weight.

 8.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims, characterized by the width of the said strip is between 5 to 30 mm.

 9.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims, characterized by the width of the said strip is between 8 to 15 mm.

 10.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims, characterized by the number of the said warp yarns or the cords (3) is 3 to 15 in a width of 10 mm.

 11.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims, characterized by a cord twisting degree of the said warp yarns (3) is between 100 and 800 twist/meter (tpm).

 12.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims, characterized by a cord twisting degree of the said warp yarns (3) is between 250 and 350 tpm.

 13.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims, characterized by a number of the said cotton weft yarns (2) is 5 to 50, preferably 10 to 20 in a strip (1) having the length of 10 cm.

 14.   A cap ply reinforcement strip (1) according to any one of the preceding claims, characterized by the said warp yarns (3) are comprising of nylon    6, PET (polyethylene terephthalate), aramide cords or hybrid cords such as PET-nylon 6.6, aramide-nylon 6.6 or aramide-PET. .
ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of poor performance and durability of cap ply reinforcement strips in pneumatic radial tires, particularly at high speeds. Traditional cap ply reinforcement strips often rely on texturized nylon weft yarns, which are known to narrow during heat setting, leading to reduced performance and potential air voids in tire manufacturing. Additionally, these strips may not provide sufficient lateral warp cord separation resistance during cutting processes, resulting in weak bonds and reduced structural integrity. The invention aims to overcome these limitations by using high linear density cotton weft yarns, which help in maintaining the integrity of the cap ply during manufacturing and improve overall tire performance.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention proposes a cap ply reinforcement strip that is produced by plain weaving warp cords with high linear density cotton weft yarns. This method eliminates the need for calendering and strip preparing stages, reducing rolling resistance and improving fuel efficiency. The strip is wound on the belt package of a radial tire, ensuring it is in direct contact with the tread rubber. The cotton weft yarns are arranged with a linear density between 400 and 2000 dtex, and the adhesive content on the strip surface is at least 10% and at most 60%. The strip is designed to prevent excessive narrowing during heat setting and to provide lateral warp cord separation resistance during cutting processes. This approach ensures a strong, durable, and performance-enhancing cap ply reinforcement strip for pneumatic radial tires.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention offers significant advantages over prior art by using high linear density cotton weft yarns, which help in maintaining the integrity of the cap ply during manufacturing and improve performance. It eliminates the need for calendering and strip preparing stages, reducing rolling resistance and fuel consumption. The strip provides strong lateral warp cord separation resistance during cutting processes, preventing bond separation and ensuring structural integrity. It also prevents excessive narrowing during heat setting, reducing the risk of air voids. The adhesive dip ensures a strong bond at contact points, enhancing the durability and performance of the cap ply reinforcement strip. The use of cotton weft yarns with a linear density between 400 and 2000 dtex allows for a balanced performance between holding warp yarns together and preventing excessive adhesive content, which is critical for maintaining tire durability and handling performance.

The invention addresses the issue of high-speed durability and stability in pneumatic vehicle tires. Traditional belt bandages often use expensive materials like aramid or polyethylene naphthalate (PEN), which are costly and difficult to process. METHOD USED
The invention involves creating a pneumatic vehicle tire with a belt bandage that includes HMLS PET reinforcements in the two side regions and PA6.6 in the central region. The belt bandage is divided into two side regions and a central region, with each region containing a bandage layer part. In the central region, the bandage layer part is reinforced with PA6.6, which has a tensile strength of over 0.35 cN/dtex at 2% elongation, over 0.70 cN/dtex at 4% elongation, and over 1.20 cN/dtex at 6% elongation. The reinforcements are preferably made of yarns and/or cords, with a fineness of 700 dtex to 1800 dtex. The HMLS PET cords are made from two 1440 dtex yarns twisted together, while PA6.6 cords are made from two twisted 1400 dtex yarns. The resulting tire has a balanced contour, optimized for high-speed performance and durability. [EP2829420A1]

title: TIRE WITH MULTIPLE STEEL BELTS AND A REINFORCEMENT LAYER
abstract: A tire includes a pair of annular beads, a body ply extending between the pair of annular beads, and at least three steel belt layers disposed above the body ply and extending axially across a portion of the body ply. The tire further includes at least one reinforcement layer disposed above the at least three steel belt layers, a circumferential tread disposed above the at least one reinforcement layer and extending axially across the tire, and a pair of sidewalls extending between each of the pair of annular beads and a pair of shoulders associated with the circumferential tread.

Current tire constructions, particularly radial tires, rely on circumferential belts and reinforcement cords that extend radially from bead to bead. These belts are typically inextensible and circumferential, with reinforcement cords that restrict belt edge movement and prevent crack growth. However, the addition of more belts increases load capacity but also introduces the risk of belt end movement and crack growth. Existing solutions like cap plies and shoulder layers are unnecessary for large trucks and buses, as they add weight and cost. The invention addresses the need for a tire that avoids these drawbacks by incorporating multiple steel belts and reinforcement layers in the crown region, which can be pre-tensioned to control growth and reduce wear. The shoulder layer is pre-tensioned during tire construction, ensuring it restricts belt growth and reduces wear. The tire may include multiple body plies, each wrapped around the beads, or not. The reinforcement layers are designed to be under tension when not in contact with the ground, helping to control growth and reduce wear. [EP4294649B1]

The invention addresses the issue of wear and rolling resistance in pneumatic vehicle tires, particularly in high-speed applications. Traditional tire designs often result in excessive wear due to overlapping strengthening elements in the lateral sections, which can lead to localized material thickening and reduced durability. Additionally, the use of PA6.6 in all sections results in a thinner calendered ply, which compromises rolling resistance and flat spotting performance. The invention aims to solve these problems by optimizing the arrangement and composition of strengthening elements to minimize wear while maintaining high-speed performance and durability. The invention involves a pneumatic vehicle tire comprising a carcass, a tread, and a belt. The belt is covered by a belt bandage that includes three sections: a central section and two lateral sections. The central section uses a strengthening element construction (x1) with a diameter of 0.30 mm and a density of 120 epdm, while the lateral sections use a higher construction (x2 or x3) with a diameter of 0.40 mm and a density of 130 epdm. The lateral sections are arranged without overlapping with the central section, ensuring that the density of strengthening elements in the central section is less than in the lateral sections. The strengthening elements in the central section are made of PA6.6, while the lateral sections are made of PA6.6 or PET. The belt bandage is formed from three parts with a central section and two lateral sections, where the lateral sections are arranged without overlapping. The strengthening elements are embedded in an unvulcanized rubber mixture, wound or coiled onto the belt, and embedded in the rubber mixture. The belt bandage is applied in the form of plies, strips, or individual elements, with the strengthening elements embedded in the rubber mixture. The lateral sections are arranged with a distance of 5 mm to 15 mm from the outer end of the widest belt ply, ensuring that the lateral sections do not overlap with the central section. The belt bandage is designed to have a total fineness of 940 dtex in the central section and 470 dtex in the lateral sections. The strengthening elements are arranged in a twist factor range of 140 to 210 for x2 cords and 10 to 80 for x1 cords. The belt bandage is applied in a manner that minimizes wear and enhances rolling resistance and flat spotting performance. [US2021031563A1]

Traditional three-proofing tires often suffer from delamination due to high-frequency flexing and stress points, leading to safety risks and reduced durability. The existing solution relies on nylon 66 as a reinforcing layer, which is prone to melting at high temperatures during vulcanization, causing delamination and compromising the tire's integrity. ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of separation of mutually adjacent components in pneumatic tires due to differing elastic moduli between the carcass ply and the bead filler apex. Conventional belt structures often use multiple reinforcement layers with unidirectional load carrying, leading to weight, cost, and performance trade-offs. The problem arises from the inability to manage the force transfer in opposite directions, especially under high-speed, runflat, or high-performance conditions, where the flexure and heating in the bead region can cause separation of the carcass ply and bead filler apex. This separation compromises the tire's durability, performance, and reliability.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention introduces a novel belt construction that replaces conventional belt layers with a single continuous reinforcement strip. This strip is composed of a continuous cord forming a zigzag pattern across the width of the crown portion of the tire. The reinforcement is designed to have a constant width of 3.0 mm to 30.0 mm and includes materials such as steel, polyester, polyamide, aramid, or fused polyester. The method involves replacing the bead filler apex and overlay with a single crown reinforcement, which is then applied radially outward of the carcass ply. This approach minimizes the number of reinforcement layers, reduces weight, and improves durability by eliminating the need for multiple belt structures.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention offers significant advantages over conventional belt structures by eliminating the need for multiple reinforcement layers, reducing weight, and improving durability. It minimizes the risk of separation between the carcass ply and bead filler apex due to the uniformity of the reinforcement. The continuous reinforcement strip provides consistent stiffness and strength, enhancing performance and reliability. The use of materials like steel, polyester, polyamide, aramid, or fused polyester allows for customization of weight and thermal properties. The method also reduces material costs, simplifies manufacturing, and improves high-speed performance by eliminating belt edges and improving crown durability. The single reinforcement strip is more flexible and easier to produce in a short period, leading to cost savings and enhanced tire functionality.

PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of durability decline in pneumatic tires when using high modulus organic fibers for string of a hat cord. Traditional methods often lead to premature failure due to compression fatigue and fracture in high modulus fibers, especially in radial directions. This results in reduced tire quality, increased risk of damage, and compromised performance at high speeds. The challenge lies in maintaining the integrity of the cord while ensuring uniform rigidity and stability in the tire's circumference. [CN106163780A]

METHOD USED
The invention involves creating a pneumatic tire with a belt ply composed of multiple rectangle cord sheets arranged parallel on the tire circumference. Each cord sheet is formed by a narrow and strip-shaped rubber cover and a specific length, arranged at an angle relative to the tire circumference. The cord sheets are formed by pasting them successively on a rigid core for building, which is then used in sulfurizing molding. The rigid core is designed to approximate the tire's outer shape, and the sulfurizing mold is placed between the core and the tire. The composite cord sheets are formed by combining a high modulus organic fiber strand (e.g., aramid fiber) with a low modulus organic fiber strand (e.g., nylon fiber), ensuring that the high modulus strand is twisted to enhance strength retention. The cord sheets are arranged to prevent overlap and ensure uniform rigidity, with specific dimensions and angles for optimal performance. The belt ply is formed by winding the cord sheets around the tire circumference, covering the rubber and ensuring the cord remains intact during manufacturing and operation. [CN106163780A]

PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
Tires are susceptible to damage from perforations and pinch shocks, which can lead to loss of inflation pressure, tire flattening, and vehicle immobilization. Traditional solutions like puncture-proofing and self-sealing products either require stopping the vehicle or fail in extreme conditions, leading to performance degradation and increased maintenance costs. The invention addresses the need for a tire that can withstand both types of damage without compromising performance or requiring frequent repairs, thereby improving reliability and user experience. [US2015375574A1]
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The tire comprises an internal wall and an external wall, with the internal wall covered by an airtight layer. A self-sealing layer is applied to this airtight layer, facing the crown. The self-sealing layer is composed of a thermoplastic stirene elastomer (TPS) and extending oil, with TPS selected from SEBS, SEPS, or SEEPS copolymers. The self-sealing layer is positioned over the airtight layer, extending over the sidewalls at least a portion of the radial distance. The carcass reinforcement is composed of thread reinforcing elements with an elongation at break (EB) and a breaking strength (BS), placed at a placement pitch (PC) and coated with rubber composition. The carcass reinforcement extends from one bead to the other, passing through the crown, and is anchored in each bead by a turn-up around an annular reinforcing structure. The additional strengthening reinforcement is placed along the return strand of the carcass reinforcement, extending between the radial end of the annular reinforcing structure and the radial end of the carcass reinforcement. abstract: Tyres for vehicle wheels having reduced environmental impact and the components thereof, in particular reinforcing structural elements such as carcass structures, belt structures, flippers and chafers, comprising elongated reinforcing elements treated with resorcinol- and formaldehyde-free cross-linkable adhesive compositions are described. These adhesive compositions comprise at least a) a rubber latex, at least b) an epoxide and at least c) a polyamine with molecular weight higher than 190 Dalton, comprising at least two amino groups selected from primary -NH2 and secondary -NH- amino groups. In the structural element, these compositions confer an adhesion between cords and compounds that is comparable if not better than the traditional RFL system in use in this sector. Furthermore, by suitably modifying the compound compositions in the reinforced structural elements and, possibly, also in the other elastomeric components of the tyre, it is possible to manufacture tyres while avoiding the use of toxic chemicals such as resorcinol and formaldehyde.

ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
Aircraft tires are subjected to extreme operating conditions including high internal pressures, tremendous loads, and high speeds. Traditional bias tires, which have alternating ply layers at 0°–45° relative to the equatorial plane, suffer from increased deflection, leading to higher heat generation and mechanical fatigue in the bead area. Radial tires, while lighter, face challenges in maintaining structural integrity and durability due to the increased deflection and potential for bead cracking or scuffing. The invention addresses these issues by providing a radial ply tire that balances durability and bending resistance, ensuring consistent performance under heavy loads and high pressures. [US2013118666A1]
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention comprises a radial ply tire with a radial carcass, tread, and crown reinforcement. The carcass is composed of plies extending from a bead core, which is wound into a central hoop. These plies are reinforced by cords oriented at 0°–45° relative to the equatorial plane, forming a radial structure. The crown reinforcement includes belt layers and strips reinforced by cords at 5°–30° angles, with a zigzag belt reinforcing structure that interwoven cords at 5°–30° angles. The bead core is made of an alloy like 6061 T, with a central wire wound into a continuous hoop. The bead area is designed with a Ra/Fr1 relationship, where Ra is the tire radius of the bead sidewall and Fr1 is the rim flange maximum radius. The bead compression ratio is less than 24%, and the ratio of the narrowest belt layer to the widest is between 0.3–0.6. The tire is mounted on a rim flange with a rim flange width between 7.75″ and 12.0R19, and the B/W ratio is between 0.63–0.7, with the rim flange width to bead width ratio between 0.84–1.0. The tire is constructed using a tubeless inner liner containing fluid or air, and the plies are made of nylon or aramid composites with specific elongation and break strength properties. The zigzag belt reinforcing structure is embedded within the belt layers, ensuring even distribution of bending forces and reducing deformation. [US2013118666A1]
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention provides radial ply tires with significantly improved durability and bending resistance, reducing heat generation and bead cracking. The bead compression ratio is less than 24%, minimizing friction and deformation. The zigzag belt reinforcing structure enhances lateral bending and reduces deformation, while the optimized B/W ratio ensures efficient load distribution. The bead area design with Ra/Fr1 relationship reduces contact pressure and improves bead durability. The tire is suitable for use in aircraft, truck, and commercial off-road applications, offering enhanced performance under high load and pressure conditions. The construction method allows for flexibility in material selection and structural design, making the tire adaptable to various applications. [US2013118666A1]

title: Overlay ply covering the belt ply for a pneumatic tire
abstract: A pneumatic tire is disclosed comprising a carcass reinforced by at least one carcass ply (12), at least one belt ply (24) disposed radially outward of the carcass ply (12) in a crown portion of the pneumatic tire (10), and at least one overlay (13) disposed radially outward of the belt ply (24) in the crown portion of the pneumatic tire (10). The overlay (13) comprises at least one composite cord (30) having at least one core filament or core yarn (32) and at least one outer metallic filament (34) wrapped around the at least one core filament or core yarn (32) such that the at least one core filament or core yarn (32) has a Young's modulus at room temperature less than the Young's modulus at room temperature of the at least one outer metallic filament (34). The at least one core filament or core yarn (32) has a diameter in the range of from 0.3 mm to 0.9 mm, alternatively from 0.45 to 0.75 mm, and a twist in the range of from 5 to 15 turns per 2.54 cm (TPI). The at least one outer metallic filament (34) is twisted about the at least one core filament or core yarn (32) with a twist in the range of from 3 to 14 turns per 2.54 cm (TPI).

The invention addresses the challenge of achieving optimal performance in runflat pneumatic tires. Conventional hybrid cords in runflat tires often fail to balance flexibility and rigidity between inflated and uninflated conditions due to uneven load distribution and poor fatigue resistance. Traditional hybrid cords are composed of low modulus core yarns and high modulus wrap yarns, which have a break point between 2% and 3% elongation, but fail to maintain consistent performance when the tire is in an uninflated state. Additionally, single carcass plies and wedge inserts in conventional runflat tires do not equally support the load, leading to uneven stress distribution and reduced overall rigidity. The invention aims to solve these issues by introducing a hybrid cord overlay that ensures uniform load distribution and enhanced fatigue resistance in both inflated and uninflated conditions. [US2011259500A1]

METHOD USED
The hybrid cord overlay is constructed by combining a low modulus core yarn with a high modulus outer metallic filament. The core yarn is selected from materials like rayon, nylon, polyamide 6, and polyethylene terephthalate (PET), with a diameter range of 0.012 to 0.035 inches and a twist range of 5 to 15 TPI. The outer metallic filament is chosen from materials such as Normal Tensile Steel, High Tensile Steel, Super Tensile Steel, Ultra Tensile Steel, Mega Tensile Steel, titanium, stainless steel, aluminum, and alloys thereof, with a diameter range of 0.04 to 0.41 mm. The core yarn is twisted about the outer filament at least 3 to 14 TPI, with a lay length of 3 to 25 mm. The overlay is formed by encapsulating the crossed cord plies between the overlay and the carcass ply, with the overlay having an axial width equal to or greater than the maximum axial width of the crossed cord plies. The overlay is reinforced with cords inclined at angles of 0° to 15° relative to the equatorial plane of the tire. The hybrid cord is made by twisting the core yarn around the outer filament, with the core yarn having a modulus less than the outer filament. The overlay is formed from at least one composite cord, with a specific ratio of core yarn to outer filament, such as 1/1, 1/2, 2/2, 3/2, 1/3, 2/3, 3/3, or 4/3. The overlay is designed to provide excellent fatigue resistance, even in the absence of complete theoretical understanding of tire mechanics. The hybrid cord is applied to the tire structure, including the carcass ply, belt structure, and wedge inserts, to ensure uniform load distribution and enhanced performance in both inflated and uninflated conditions. [US2011259500A1]

The overlay is designed to be encapsulated between the carcass ply and belt structure, ensuring that the crossed cord plies are properly supported. The hybrid cord is made from materials with specific properties, such as 1/1, 1/2, 2/2, 3/2, 1/3, 2/3, 3/3, or 4/3 ratios, which optimize performance. The overlay is also made from materials with specific parameters, such as linear density, twist, and lay length, to ensure optimal performance. abstract: The invention relates to a vehicle tyre comprising at least two bracing plies intersecting at an angle, and a bracing bandage. The reinforcements of at least one bracing ply consist of a non-metallic material, preferably rayon, each bracing ply having a tension of < 17.500 N per dm of width, with a pre-determined extension of 1%, and the reinforcements of the bracing plies are at an angle of between 18° and 45° to the peripheral direction of the tyre. Traditional symmetrical tires fail to provide adequate handling, grip, and durability in asymmetric environments, leading to reduced performance and increased wear. The invention aims to enhance tire properties by introducing an asymmetric outer contour and a bandage design that dynamically adjusts to different speed ranges, ensuring optimal performance across various driving scenarios. METHOD USED
The tire comprises a carcass ply, a tread, bead regions with bead cores and core profiles, side walls, a multilayer belt between the tread and carcass ply, and a belt bandage. The tread has a circumferential grooves and is designed with a ratio of radius R1 to the nominal width NB of 1.8 to 5.0 for the first half and 1.2 to 2.5 for the second half. The tread width TW45 is slightly larger than the tire clearance in the ground when mounted on a rim and larger under pressure. The bandage is composed of two bandage layers: one extending in the first half of the tire and beyond the geometric center plane into the second half, and another extending similarly. The bandage layers are made of rubber embedded cords, preferably nylon, with a linear force elongation curve. The bandage is constructed with a hybrid cord that includes a cord core of nylon and aramid threads, providing a steep, linear force elongation curve. The bandage is designed to cover the belt and extend beyond the geometric center plane into the second half of the tire, ensuring dynamic growth and improved durability. The side walls are designed with different stiffness levels, with the first half being stiffer for the interior and the second half being stiffer for the exterior, enhancing tire performance and durability. [EP2048005A1]
ai_advantages:

The invention provides significant advantages over traditional symmetrical tires by optimizing tire performance for asymmetric driving conditions. The asymmetric outer contour adjusts the ground contact area and tire behavior, enhancing handling, grip, and durability. The bandage design ensures dynamic growth and improved durability at high and low speeds, with the hybrid cord providing a steep, linear force elongation curve. The asymmetric side walls and bandage layers ensure that the tire is not overly stressed in the shoulder area, reducing wear and improving overall performance. The tire can be mounted on the vehicle such that the first half faces the interior and the second half faces the exterior, ensuring uniform pressure distribution and optimal handling in cornering scenarios. The invention also allows for the tire to be designed for different speed ranges, providing consistent performance across various driving conditions. [EP2048005A1]

Traditional tires often fail to provide the necessary dynamic growth characteristics at varying speeds, leading to inconsistent performance and reduced wear. The invention aims to achieve a tire that performs well in lower-speed ranges (80–90 km/h) with good aquaplaning, a flat contour in the middle-speed range (100–160 km/h) for low abrasion, and a high-speed performance at speeds beyond 200 km/h with a circular contour for durability. This is particularly important for high-speed applications where minimizing water displacement and maximizing tire longevity is critical.

title: MONOPLY PNEUMATIC RUN-FLAT TIRE
abstract: A mono-ply pneumatic run-flat tire is provided to enable a bending behavior of component parts of the run-flat tire to improve comfort and an adjustment function, and also improve a run-flat function. A mono-ply pneumatic run-flat tire(10) comprises a single carcass ply(12), at least one belt ply, and at least one insert(20). The at least one belt ply is disposed at an outer side with respect to radial directions of the carcass ply at a crown part of the tire. The at least one insert is disposed at a sidewall part adjacent to the carcass ply to support weight of the tire so that the tire even in an underinflated state can be operated. The carcass ply comprises at least one composite cord. The composite cord comprises at least two first yarns spirally winding at least one second yarn. The first and the second yarns have respectively different elasticity modulus. More particularly, the first yarns have greater modulus than the second yarn.

ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the challenge of balancing high-speed durability with good handling performance in pneumatic tires. Traditional tires often fail to maintain optimal ground contact area and crown curvature at high speeds due to the limitations of material properties and structural design. The problem is exacerbated by the need to manage stress concentrations and ensure consistent tire performance across varying speeds and temperatures. The invention aims to resolve this by introducing a novel crown structure that enhances both the tire's ability to handle at high speeds and its durability under these conditions.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention constructs a pneumatic tire with a crown structure that includes a first reinforcing ply with parallel, angled reinforcements oriented at an angle α (10° to 45°) relative to the circumferential direction. This ply is anchored in the bead structure to resist tension during inflation. A second reinforcing ply with high modulus at high stress cords is placed radially outside the first ply, preferably in the center part of the crown, to enhance the tire's ability to flatten the transverse curvature of the outer contour at low and moderate speeds. The third reinforcing ply with low modulus at high stress cords is positioned axially under the central rib of the tread to reduce static belt breaker stresses. The cords are made of high elastic modulus at high stress organic fibers, such as nylon or aramid, and are preferably helically wound with a laying pitch p of 0.5 to 0.9 mm. The cords are chosen to have a tensile strength at high strain and high temperature inferior to 1.5 daN, ensuring negligible impact at high speeds. The tire is designed with a bead filler having high creeping resistance at high stress and temperature, and the carcass structure is anchored in the bead portion to resist tension. The full width ply is placed radially under the breaker belt to improve the hoop effect of the cords. The tire is built on a rigid core with a substantially cylindrical outer contour, and the cords are chosen based on their stress-strain characteristics and temperature stability.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention provides a tire with significantly improved handling performance at high speeds while maintaining high durability. The optimized crown structure ensures a consistent ground contact area and crown curvature, enhancing dry and wet handling capabilities. The use of high modulus at high stress cords in the second reinforcement plies allows the tire to flatten the transverse curvature at low and moderate speeds, improving wear performance. The low tensile strength cords in the third reinforcement plies minimize their impact at high speeds, preserving the tire's center length and maintaining a rectangular or oval ground contact area. The tire's design also reduces static belt breaker stresses, improving overall performance and safety. The method allows for independent adjustment of tire properties at low and moderate speeds, enhancing adaptability to different operational conditions.

ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of low strength utilization in hybrid cords used for tire reinforcement. Traditional nylon/aramid hybrid cords suffer from uneven twist index differences between aramid and nylon fibers, leading to reduced fatigue resistance and performance. This problem is exacerbated by the need for high-performance tires at high speeds, where deformation of the belt part is critical. The invention aims to solve this by creating a hybrid cord with an unbalanced structure that ensures high strength and fatigue resistance, even when subjected to external forces.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The hybrid cord is composed of a first yarn with a low modulus (e.g., nylon filaments with a fineness of 800 to 1700 denier) and a second yarn with a higher modulus (e.g., aramid filaments with a fineness of 1000 to 2000 denier). The first yarn is pre-twisted and the second yarn is not. These yarns are simultaneously twisted in a single machine, forming a plied yarn. The twist count of the first yarn is 3 to 25% of the second yarn's twist count. For example, if the second yarn has a twist count of 200 TPM, the first yarn has a twist count of 60 TPM. The first yarn is pre-twisted and the second yarn is not. The first under twisted yarn is formed by twisting the first yarn and the second yarn simultaneously. The second under twisted yarn is formed by twisting the second yarn and the first yarn simultaneously. The first lower twisted yarn and the second lower twisted yarn are spun together to form a plied yarn. The hybrid cord is then immersed in an adhesive drying and heat treating process, ensuring the twist index ratio is within 0.94 to 1.24. This method allows for a balanced strength and fatigue resistance in the hybrid cord, improving its performance in high-speed tire applications.

It overcomes the issue of functional imbalance in traditional hybrid cords by creating an unbalanced structure through precise twist count and yarn fineness control. The method improves strength utilization rate, adhesiveness, and overall performance, making it suitable for high-performance tires and electric vehicle tires. The use of a direct cabler allows for improved productivity and reduced manufacturing costs, while the precise twist count and yarn fineness control ensure uniform properties and enhanced durability.

PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of low strength utilization ratio in traditional hybrid cords used in high-performance tires and electric vehicle tires. These cords often fail to maintain the required physical properties due to the inherent differences in modulus between the first and second yarns. The problem arises when the pre-twisted first yarn has a lower modulus, while the untwisted second yarn has a higher modulus, leading to uneven twist indices and reduced overall performance. This results in lower strength, fatigue resistance, and adhesive force, which compromises the durability and riding comfort of the tire during high-speed operation.

METHOD USED
The invention involves creating a hybrid cord by combining a first yarn (lower modulus) and a second yarn (higher modulus). The first yarn is pre-twisted, typically by 3% to 25% of its first twist number, while the second yarn is untwisted and twisted in a different direction. The pre-twisted first yarn is selected from conventional nylon 6, nylon 66, nylon 6.10, nylon 5,6, and nylon 4,10, with preferred deniers of 800 to 1700 denier. The second yarn is selected from aramid, aromatic polyamide, wholly aromatic polyester, and their mixtures, with deniers of 1000 to 2000 denier. The first primary twisted yarn is formed by twisting the pre-twisted first yarn, while the second primary twisted yarn is formed by twisting the untwisted second yarn. These two yarns are then combined in a single twisting machine, with the first and second yarns twisted simultaneously in the same direction. The resulting ply yarn is dried and heat-treated to achieve the desired strength and fatigue resistance properties. The hybrid cord is then used as a cap ply in high-performance tires and electric vehicle tires to enhance durability and stability during high-speed operation.

By pre-twisting the first yarn and simultaneously twisting the second yarn, the method ensures a balanced twist index ratio, enhancing the performance of the tire. This approach reduces the need for multiple twisting machines, improving production efficiency and reducing manufacturing costs. The hybrid cord is designed to maintain high strength utilization ratios and excellent fatigue resistance, making it ideal for high-performance tires and electric vehicle tires. The method also minimizes the risk of uneven twist indices, ensuring consistent performance and reliability in high-speed environments.

The invention addresses the issue of poor processability and uniformity in pneumatic tires when using conventional tire blind fabrics. Traditional tire blind fabrics, which use high rigidity organic fiber cords for warp threads and cotton spun yarns for weft threads, suffer from instability in widths and variations in warp yarn count during rolling and slitting. This results in inconsistent tire tread uniformity, reduced high-speed durability, and increased road noise. The invention aims to solve these problems by enhancing the processability and uniformity of the blind fabric during manufacturing and tire assembly.

METHOD USED
The tire blind fabric comprises multiple warp threads arranged in parallel and weft threads woven to cross the warp threads at a low density. The warp threads are organic fiber cords containing PET or aramid fibers, with a total fineness in the range of 1800 dtex to 5000 dtex. The weft threads are cotton spun yarns with a fineness of 150 dtex to 350 dtex and a density of 2.0 threads/50 mm to 4.0 threads/50 mm. The fabric is treated with an adhesive composition containing an epoxy compound before rubber coating, which stabilizes the fabric and reduces variations in warp yarn count. The treated fabric is then heat-treated in a dry zone at 100°C to 150°C and a normalization zone at 225°C to 255°C. The tire is assembled with a carcass layer, belt layer, and belt cover layer, each made of the same blind fabric. The belt cover layer is formed by spirally winding a strip material of rubber-coated cord fabric around the belt layer, ensuring the belt layer does not rise when the tire rolls, improving high-speed durability and reducing road noise.

Traditional aviation tires often experience blowouts during takeoff and landing, leading to potential accidents or emergency landings. The tread is radially outward from the carcass, and the sidewall extends radially outward to a shoulder adjacent to the tread. The reinforcing structure is positioned radially between the carcass and the tread. The reinforcing structure includes an overlapping spiral wound strip with a uniform width. The belt reinforcing layer is formed by coating organic fiber cords, which are hybridized by twisting aramid yarns (e.g., para-aramid or meta-aramid) and nylon yarns (e.g., nylon 6, 66, or 46). The organic fiber cords are aligned and covered with rubber, preferably in a ratio (Sr/Sc) of 1.5 to 2.0, where Sr is the rubber cross-sectional area and Sc is the cord cross-sectional area. The rubber cross-sectional area is calculated using the formula: Sr/Sc = (load LASE5% at 5% elongation of the cord × cord count × number of belt reinforcing layers) / (load LASE0.5% at 0.5% elongation of the belt cord × cosθ × cord count × number of belt layers). The ratio is set to ensure optimal performance. The belt reinforcing layer is wound in a spiral shape on the belt layer, and the raw tire is vulcanized and molded to form the final tire. The belt layer is formed by covering belt cords with rubber, while the belt reinforcing layer is formed by coating organic fiber cords with rubber. The rubber is applied in a way that enhances the binding force and rigidity of the belt layer, preventing belt lifting, diameter growth, and edge distortion caused by centrifugal forces during high-speed travel.

By increasing the belt cord angle to 30-40 degrees, the tire retains its rigidity in the circumferential direction, preventing ground contact shape deterioration. The hybrid organic fiber cords enhance binding force and durability, ensuring the tire remains stable during high-speed travel. The precise coating and alignment of the organic fiber cords with rubber improve the tire's overall performance, making it suitable for various applications including passenger vehicle tires. The method ensures optimal balance between performance and durability, offering a reliable solution for enhancing tire performance in high-speed environments.

ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the challenge of developing high-performance tires for sports cars and motorcycles using recycled plastic filaments. Traditional tires with fossil-derived plastic materials suffer from inferior mechanical properties, such as toughness and breaking load, compared to conventional tires. The need arises to create tires that maintain high performance and durability while incorporating environmentally friendly materials, as fossil-derived plastics are often associated with environmental concerns. The invention aims to overcome these limitations by enabling the use of recycled plastic filaments in textile reinforcing cords, which can be mixed with non-recycled plastic filaments to enhance mechanical performance without compromising environmental sustainability.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention involves the production of a textile reinforcing cord comprising one or more structural components. The reinforcing cord is composed of one or more yarns, each consisting of filaments made of recycled plastic material (e.g., PET) and non-recycled plastic material (e.g., nylon, PEEK, or polyketone). These filaments are at least partially mixed, with the recycled filaments forming at least a portion of the total weight of the yarn. The textured yarns are obtained by twisting two single yarns, one of which is made of recycled plastic and the other of non-recycled plastic. The mixed yarns are then combined to form a reinforcing cord. The reinforcing cord is structured with a radial carcass structure, a cross belt structure, and a zero-degree reinforcing layer. The radial carcass structure includes reinforcing cords oriented in a substantially axial direction, while the cross belt structure includes reinforcing cords oriented in a radially external position. The zero-degree reinforcing layer is wound in a substantially circumferential direction. The reinforcing cords are treated to ensure they adhere to the elastomeric material of the tire, using an adhesive composition that is compatible with the material. The process also involves adjusting the quantity and density of recycled plastic filaments in the yarn to optimize mechanical performance and environmental impact.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention offers significant advantages over prior methods by enabling the use of recycled plastic filaments in textile reinforcing cords without compromising mechanical properties. This reduces environmental impact while maintaining the necessary performance characteristics for high-performance tires. The method allows for precise control over the mechanical properties of the reinforcing cords, ensuring compatibility with the adhesion requirements of the tire. The use of textured yarns with recycled and non-recycled filaments enhances the uniform distribution of recycled material, improving durability and longevity of the tire. Additionally, the method minimizes the need for SSP treatments or excessive twisting, which can degrade the mechanical behavior of the reinforcing cords. The resulting tires are lighter, more responsive to stresses, and more environmentally friendly, making them suitable for both sports cars and motorcycles.

METHOD USED
The invention involves creating a tire with a carcass ply, a tread, and an overlay ply strip. The overlay ply strip is composed of multiple polyamide monofilament plies, each with a density ranging from 300 dtex to 470 dtex. These plies are twisted together using between 1 and 2 twists per inch to form the cord. The cord is then embedded within the rubber composition of the tire, typically in the belt plies and overlay plies. The ply strip is wound around the tire in a circumferential direction, covering the radially outermost belt ply below the tread. The cords are arranged in parallel, preferably beside each other, to enhance reinforcement. The ply strip may extend over the belt plies at an angle of between 0° and 5° with the equatorial plane of the tire. The cord is also coated with an adhesive to enhance adhesion and improve flex fatigue resistance. The ply strip is made in a fabric calendar unit, where multiple essentially parallel cords are coated with a layer of rubber composition and then embedded. The invention addresses the challenge of achieving high-performance, lightweight, and durable tyres for sports automobiles and motorcycles. Traditional tyres often suffer from insufficient adhesion to the ground, leading to reduced efficiency in high-speed driving and poor performance under lateral stresses. Additionally, conventional metallic reinforcing cords are heavy and may cause hysteresis issues, which can affect tyre longevity and performance. The invention aims to resolve these issues by integrating both monofilament and multifilament textile fibers into a single hybrid reinforcing cord, which enhances adhesion, resistance to compression and bending stresses, and reduces hysteresis while maintaining structural integrity. The hybrid reinforcing cord is constructed by intertwining monofilament textile wires with at least one multifilament textile yarn. Monofilament wires are typically made of aliphatic polyamide or polyester fibres, with diameters ranging from 0.1 mm to 1 mm, preferably between 0.2 mm and 0.5 mm. These wires are twisted together with the multifilament yarn using a predetermined twisting pitch, which can be between 2 mm and 20 mm, preferably 3 mm to 10 mm. The multifilament yarn is composed of aromatic polyamide, aliphatic polyamide, polyester, or other aromatic fibers, with a linear density of at least 400 dTex, more preferably 800 dTex, and lower than 4500 dTex, more preferably 4000 dTex. The hybrid cord is arranged in a radial structure, with the outer surface defined by both monofilament and multifilament components. This design allows for efficient stress transfer and improved adhesion to the elastomeric material, making the hybrid cord suitable for use in both sports automobiles and motorcycles. The cord is applied to the support structure and tread band, with the zero-degree reinforcing layer also incorporating the hybrid cord to enhance structural performance and reduce interference with RFID and sensor signals. title: Low-rolling-resistance tire made of aramid fiber nylon 66
abstract: The invention discloses a low-rolling-resistance tire made of aramid fiber nylon 66. The low-rolling-resistance tire comprises a lining surface, a tire body, a tire ring, a tire sidewall, a belt ply, a cap ply, a tread, a bead filler and bead rings, contact position of the tire sidewall and the tire ring is filled with the bead filler, the bead rings are mounted on the outer side of the lining surface, and the tire ring, the tire sidewall, the belt ply, the cap ply and the tread are integrated on the lining surface from inside to outside. According to the low-rolling-resistance tire, aramid fiber/nylon 66 and a rubberized cord fabric are compounded, so that common steel wires and cap belts are replaced, riding comfort of tires can be improved, rolling resistance of the tires is reduced, oil consumption is reduced, high speed endurance performance of the tires can be improved, vulcanizing time is shortened, the problem of flat spots of the tires is effectively improved, and the aramid fiber/nylon 66 replaces steel belts and nylon cap belts. Compared with a common passenger car radial tire of same specification, the weight is reduced by about 8%, rolling resistance is reduced by about 18%, and the retread frequency of the tires is improved.

ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of high rolling resistance in traditional tires, particularly those made with aramid fiber as the framework material. Prior art tires suffer from significant rolling resistance, leading to increased fuel consumption, environmental pollution, and reduced tire longevity due to flat spot problems and pierce tap beam issues. These problems are exacerbated by the high density of steel wire in common radial tire frames, which results in poor mechanical properties, high cost, and inefficiency in tire production. The invention aims to provide a tire that offers improved performance, reduced rolling resistance, and enhanced environmental benefits by replacing traditional steel wire components with a composite cord fabric made from aramid fiber and nylon66 fiber.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention proposes a method for creating a low rolling resistance tire using a composite cord fabric composed of aramid fiber and nylon66 fiber. This fabric replaces traditional steel wire components in the tire structure, including the belt, band, and hat, thereby reducing rolling resistance and improving tire performance. The method involves forming the tire with a specific arrangement of internal and external components, such as interior facings, carcass, tyre bead, sidewall, belt, band, tyre surface, triangle rubber, and wire loop, each filled with the respective material. The belt angle and cap strip width are optimized using finite element analysis software to achieve the desired mechanical properties and reduce rolling resistance. This approach enhances the tire's comfort, reduces fuel consumption, and improves tire longevity by addressing the shortcomings of traditional steel wire-based tires.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention offers significant advantages over prior art tires. It reduces rolling resistance by about 18%, leading to lower fuel consumption and improved fuel efficiency. The tire also minimizes environmental pollution by reducing the use of steel wire, which is a major source of emissions. The composite cord fabric provides enhanced mechanical properties, including high flexibility, strength, and low density, making it more durable and cost-effective. The tire's structure is optimized for high-speed performance and long-term durability, with a weight reduction of up to 8% compared to traditional steel wire-based radial tires. Additionally, the tire's design improves tire rebuilding numbers and reduces the risk of flat spot issues, extending its service life and enhancing overall tire performance. The use of aramid fiber/nylon66 fiber composite cord fabric also allows for better thermal management and improved tire stability, making it a superior alternative to conventional materials.

The problem addressed by the invention is that of providing a reinforcement layer for elastomeric products which exhibits a relatively high tensile force value for an elongation of 4% or more and which exhibits relatively low shrinkage based on linear density of the reinforcement. This is achieved in that the cords are hybrid cords having precisely three yarns, in that the hybrid cord has the first yarn and a second yarn made of HMLS-PET, in that the hybrid cord has a first yarn or a second yarn as third yarn, and in that the linear density of each hybrid cord is at least 5000 dtex.

PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of insufficient tensile force and high shrinkage in traditional reinforcement layers for pneumatic tires and elastomeric products. These layers often fail to meet the requirements for ultrahigh speed use, where centrifugal forces must be effectively concentrated without compromising dimensional stability or flattening behavior. Current solutions, such as single or double-layer bandages, either use excessive material or exhibit poor adhesion and shrinkage, leading to reduced performance and increased rolling resistance. The invention aims to provide a reinforcement layer that balances these issues by using asymmetric hybrid cords with precise three-yarn configurations and optimized linear density.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention involves creating a reinforcement layer for elastomeric products by embedding hybrid cords into an unvulcanized rubber mixture. The hybrid cords consist of three yarns: a first yarn made of polyamide (PA 6.6), a second yarn made of HMLS PET, and a third yarn. The ends of all yarns are twisted together to form the hybrid cord. The linear density of each yarn is at least 5000 dtex, with a preferred range of 1000 to 2500 dtex, particularly 1500 to 2200 dtex. The thread density within the reinforcement layer is 50 to 90 epdm, preferably 60 to 80 epdm. The hybrid cords are embedded into the elastomeric material using an adhesive impregnation system, such as RFL dip, to ensure strong adhesion. The reinforcement layer is applied to the carcass of a pneumatic tire, bead region, or other elastomeric components, providing enhanced dimensional stability and ultrahigh speed functionality. The hybrid cords are arranged in a specific configuration to ensure optimal force/elongation behavior, with the thread density and yarn density tailored to meet the requirements of the tire's design and performance.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention offers significant advantages over prior methods by providing a reinforcement layer with enhanced tensile force for elongation of 4% or more and lower shrinkage based on linear density. This results in improved dimensional stability and reduced flattening behavior under load. The hybrid cords allow for the use of a single layer in belt bandage applications, reducing material usage and rolling resistance. The asymmetric structure of the hybrid cords also minimizes internal stresses and improves durability. The method ensures strong adhesion to elastomeric materials through an adhesive impregnation system, making the reinforcement layer suitable for high-speed pneumatic tires and other elastomeric products. The invention achieves a balance between strength, adhesion, and material efficiency, making it highly effective for ultrahigh speed applications.

title: The Radial Tire for Passenger Car
abstract: The present invention relates to a radial pneumatic tire having a flatness ratio of 0.65 or less, comprising a pair of parallel bead cores, at least one radial carcass layer wound around the bead cores, a belt layer laminated on the outer circumferential side of the carcass layer, And a cap ply formed in a circumferential direction on the outer circumferential side of the belt layer, wherein the cap ply has two layers, the aramid cord is located inside the circumference, and the nylon 66 cord encircles all or part of the aramid cord The radial pneumatic tire being manufactured by being positioned at an upper portion of an aramid cord. ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of tire temperature rise and energy loss caused by the use of materials like nylon 66, which suffer from heat shrinkage and reduced physical properties at high temperatures. These factors lead to increased tire size, reduced rotational inertia, and higher energy consumption, negatively impacting vehicle performance and safety. The challenge is to develop a cap ply that maintains tire shape stability, prevents size expansion, and reduces energy loss while maintaining material integrity and heat resistance.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention involves creating a radial tire with a cap ply made of two layers: an aramid cord positioned inside the circumference and a nylon 66 cord wrapped around the aramid cord in the upper portion. The cap ply is produced by first spinning a nylon 66 high strength fiber using a spin draw process, which involves melting the polymer, passing it through multiple high defect rollers, and stretching, heat fixing, and relaxing it to achieve a modulus of elasticity at the breaking site of 40 g/d or less. The aramid yarn is similarly produced through a dry wet spinning process, where the aromatic polyamide is spun with a specific air layer and coagulation speed to ensure a uniform fiber structure. The raw cord is then dipped in an adhesive liquid containing resocinol, formalin, and sodium hydroxide, which is aged at 25°C for 5 hours to maintain solid content. The dip cord is dried at 120–150°C for 180–220 seconds, then stretched to 1–2% in the drying process. The cap ply is applied to the upper portion of the belt structure, which includes a cut belt ply with two belt cords and a belt cord reinforcing structure. The cap ply is then cured at 130–240°C for 50–90 seconds to enhance heat resistance and reduce energy loss. The resulting tire maintains a flatness ratio of 0.65 or less, ensuring high shape stability and low rotational inertia, thus improving vehicle safety and performance.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention provides a radial tire with a cap ply that significantly reduces tire temperature rise and energy loss. The aramid cord, when wrapped around the nylon 66 cord, enhances heat resistance and maintains tire shape stability. The cap ply structure minimizes tire size expansion, improves rotational inertia, and reduces flat spot formation, leading to better handling performance and durability. The use of an adhesive liquid ensures strong adhesion to rubber, while the precise manufacturing process ensures uniform fiber properties, resulting in a tire that is both safe and efficient for high-speed driving.

ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of energy loss and tire temperature rise caused by high deformation recovery in tire cords during axial loading. Traditional cap ply materials, such as nylon 66, suffer from significant shrinkage and poor adhesion, leading to increased tire size, reduced rotational inertia, and higher fuel consumption. The challenge lies in developing a cap ply that maintains tire shape stability, suppresses tire temperature, and enhances durability without compromising structural integrity or adhesion properties.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention involves creating a hybrid cap ply by combining aramid fibers with PET multifilaments in a double structure. Aramid fibers are spun at 1500 denier / twin, with a tensile strength maintained at 200 g. These fibers are then stretched at 360 TPM to produce a raw cord. The raw cord is dip-coated with an adhesive liquid containing 29.4% resorcinol, 255.5% water, 37% formalin, and 10% sodium hydroxide. The mixture is reacted at 25°C for 5 hours, followed by heat treatment at 249°C for 1 minute. The resulting hybrid cord is then dried at 160°C for 2 minutes and heat-treated again. The cap ply is applied to the tire's outer circumferential side, with aramid fibers reinforced in parallel to the tire's circumferential direction. The belt structure includes two cut belt plies wound at 20° to 16° angles, and the cap ply is reinforced on the upper part of the belt structure. The cap ply is composed of a single layer or two layers of hybrid cord, with the edge ply reinforced in parallel to the circumferential direction. The cap ply is applied to the tire's bead regions, which are non-stretchable and reinforced with high-strength steel wires. The cap ply is designed to have a shrinkage rate of less than 1.0% and an E S value of 4.0% or less, ensuring high durability and structural stability.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention provides a cap ply that significantly reduces energy loss and tire temperature rise by using aramid fibers with high initial modulus and short shrinkage rate. The hybrid cap ply enhances tire durability and structural stability, preventing tire size increase during operation. It also improves adhesion properties, ensuring strong bonding between the cap ply and rubber. The cap ply maintains tire shape stability, reducing rotational inertia and improving fuel economy. The use of PET multifilaments with low modulus ensures thermal resistance, while the double structure of the cap ply increases mechanical strength and fatigue resistance. This results in a more efficient and durable pneumatic tire for passenger cars.

ai_problem:
PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the challenge of improving the performance of radial tires by enhancing the edge ply with a hybrid dipped cord composed of nylon 66 and polyketone multifilaments. Traditional cap ply used in passenger cars often suffers from reduced strength and fatigue resistance due to low strength of polyketone multifilaments and poor adhesion. The invention aims to overcome these limitations by combining high-strength nylon 66 with polyketone multifilaments to create a hybrid dipped cord that maintains shape stability, adhesion, and strength retention, thereby improving tire safety, ride comfort, and fuel economy.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention involves the production of a hybrid dipped cord comprising nylon 66 and polyketone multifilaments. The nylon 66 yarn is produced using a spin draw method, where a melt is extruded through a spinneret, then stretched, heat fixed, and relaxed while passing through multiple pairs of high defect rollers. The temperature of the rollers is adjusted to 140 to 280°C, with a preferred range of 160 to 270°C. The polyketone multifilaments are produced by dissolving a polyketone polymer containing 90 mol% or more of ketone units in an aqueous solution of resorcinol, extruding it through a spinneret, and stretching it in a coagulating bath with a ratio of methanol to resorcinol of 9:70. The stretching process is carried out in a hot air heating type method, with a preferred temperature range of 140 to 280°C. The polyketone yarn is then dried at 100°C or higher, preferably 150°C or higher, and processed through an interlace nozzle to improve flatness and collecting properties. The final hybrid cord is wound into a radial tire, where it forms a circumferential reinforcing layer on the edge portion of the tire. The hybrid cord is characterized by a fineness of nylon 66 multifilament of 1,260 denier and polyketone multifilament of 1,000 denier, ensuring optimal strength and adhesion properties. The hybrid cord is applied to the edge ply of the radial tire, providing enhanced shape stability, adhesion, and strength retention, thereby improving tire performance and safety.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention provides significant advantages over prior methods by combining high-strength nylon 66 with polyketone multifilaments to create a hybrid dipped cord that maintains shape stability, adhesion, and strength retention. This hybrid cord enhances tire safety, ride comfort, and fuel economy by improving the edge ply's performance. The hybrid cord's high strength and low strength of polyketone multifilaments are balanced to ensure optimal physical properties. The method allows for precise control over the polyketone content and stretching parameters, resulting in a hybrid cord with superior adhesion and strength retention. The hybrid cord's application to radial tires improves the tire's ability to maintain shape under temperature changes, enhancing overall performance and durability.

PROBLEM BEING SOLVED
The invention addresses the issue of high-speed durability and low flatspot feature in pneumatic radial tires. Traditional cap ply reinforcement materials, such as nylon 6.6 or polyethylene terephthalate (PET) cords, suffer from two main disadvantages: insufficient modulus for high-speed performance and significant thermal shrinkage during cooling, leading to flatspot formation. These issues compromise the tire's ability to maintain structural integrity under high-speed conditions and temperature fluctuations, especially when the belt edge is subjected to centrifugal forces. The invention aims to resolve these problems by providing a hybrid cap ply reinforcement system that enhances durability and reduces flatspot formation. [US2017080757A1]

The hybrid cap ply reinforcement layer is constructed by twisting polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and nylon 6.6 multifilament yarns in a specific Z or S direction. The hybrid cords are then wound spirally around the belt, forming a strip with an angle of 0 to 5 degrees relative to the equatorial plane. The hybrid cords are also coated with rubber or not, depending on the application. The cap ply reinforcement layer is wound around the belt, with the width of the layer matching or exceeding the belt width. The number of cords in a 10 mm width layer is between 5 and 20, with the linear density of nylon 6.6 yarns (63) being less than that of PET yarns (62). The linear density of PET yarns is typically 1440 dtex, while nylon 6.6 is 1400 dtex. The heat treatment process ensures that the hybrid cords maintain their structural integrity and resistance to thermal stress during high-speed operations. [US2017080757A1]

The hybrid cap ply reinforcement system offers significant advantages over traditional methods. It provides enhanced high-speed durability by increasing the thermal shrinkage force and modulus of the hybrid cords, which resist tire growth caused by centrifugal forces. The system also reduces flatspot formation due to the improved thermal stability of the hybrid cords. Additionally, the use of a belt edge reinforcement layer further supports the cap ply layer, ensuring consistent performance and preventing detachment. The hybrid cords are more resistant to fatigue failure compared to single-layer nylon or PET materials, making them suitable for high-speed applications. This combination of materials and processes results in a more durable and reliable pneumatic radial tire, suitable for demanding driving conditions. [US2017080757A1]

Traditional methods rely on reinforcing structures like inclined belts, which increase cornering force but also introduce load dependency issues due to the need for separate reinforcing materials and external handling. These methods also result in higher manufacturing costs and susceptibility to external forces, which can damage the reinforcing material, compromising tire integrity.
ai_method:
METHOD USED
The invention introduces a pneumatic tire design that reduces load dependency by integrating a cord into the tire structure without requiring separate reinforcing materials. It utilizes two inclined belt layers within the tire width direction, where one layer is wider than the other, to maintain cornering force while minimizing load variation. The key steps involve defining the width ratio of the two belt layers, ensuring the tire equator has a specific rigidity ratio, and adjusting the inclination angle of the cord to optimize performance. This method allows for efficient cornering force generation without external reinforcement, thus improving both stability and noise performance.
ai_advantages:
ADVANTAGES
The invention significantly reduces load dependency in cornering force, enhancing steering stability and performance. It eliminates the need for separate reinforcing materials, lowering manufacturing costs and improving tire integrity. The dual-layer belt design ensures optimal rigidity and cornering force while maintaining noise performance. The controlled inclination angles of the cord layers help in managing vibration modes and noise radiation, making the tire suitable for high-speed applications and passenger vehicles. The method is cost-effective, efficient, and durable, providing a reliable solution for pneumatic tire design.
